common.effective date: The date on which the second party signs the final fixed agreement. No backdating or exploitation licence before both parties sign.
common.term: Twelve months from the effective date, with no automatic renewal. Any extension requires written agreement by both parties. Previously incurred reporting and payment duties survive expiry. This duration is a proposed business choice requiring approval.
common.territory: Worldwide, limited to the territories and listening services approved in the release schedule and legally available through the selected distribution provider.
common.rights: The artist retains master ownership. A non-exclusive licence permits distribution, delivery, reproduction and necessary use of approved artwork, metadata, name and release material solely to administer and promote the recordings in Schedule A during the term. Sublicensing is limited to necessary distribution and listening-service partners. Publishing, songwriting, merchandising, live performance, sync licensing, AI training and unrelated recordings are excluded unless separately agreed. No new exploitation is authorized after licence expiry, except separately agreed migration handling and accounting for previously generated receipts.
common.deductions: No upfront base distribution fee, undisclosed administration fee or automatic recoupment. Deduct only documented distributor or listening-service commissions, attributable refunds and reversals, and legally required withholding from covered receipts, without double-counting amounts already netted by the payer. Any additional artist-paid or recoupable expense requires prior written approval of its amount, cap and treatment. Label-funded non-recoupable costs do not reduce the artist allocation. The written offer must identify the selected distributor's actual charges before acceptance.
common.contributors: No contributor payment allocation is created by a credit or this agreement alone. Disclose contributors and existing obligations before release. Any payment split requires a separate signed schedule identifying the recipient, work, percentage, dates and revenue basis. Such allocations come only from the Artist Pool and cannot silently reduce the label share. No assumption that contributors are absent is made.
common.reporting payment: Quarterly statements for actual settled receipts, within 30 calendar days after quarter end; payment of undisputed amounts within 30 calendar days after the statement once valid payment and required tax details are provided. Proposed settlement currency: EUR; no contractual minimum payout. Identify receipts, source currency, actual exchange treatment, adjustments, deductions and both allocations. Estimates are not payable income. Queries must receive a reasoned response with available supporting records; any correction is included in the next statement. Reasonable inspection of relevant accounting records may be arranged confidentially on written notice. No automatic forfeiture of a claim or disputed amount. Reporting and settlement of later receipts survive termination. These timing and currency choices require approval and operational capacity review.
common.tax: Each party remains responsible for taxes and reporting legally applicable to its own income and status. Identify legally required withholding and available supporting evidence in the statement. Do not infer tax residency, VAT status, exemption or a tax rate. Confirm required tax information before invoicing or payment; no tax exemption is promised.
common.responsibilities: The artist supplies release-ready audio, artwork, metadata, credits and the rights or permissions necessary for the accepted use; disclose samples, covers, contributors and competing licences. The label records technical checks and obtains artist approval of final release data before delivery. Missing clearances prevent release. Material changes, extra work and costs require written approval. The label uses approved assets only within the agreed scope and protects confidential personal and unreleased material, sharing it only as necessary with service providers or as legally required. Both parties promptly notify material rights or security issues and cooperate on corrections. No blanket unlimited indemnity, waiver of mandatory rights or unreviewed liability cap is introduced. Formal notices go to the verified contact addresses recorded in the final agreement; material variations require a new accepted version.
common.termination: Either party may give 30 calendar days written notice to end the relationship. For a remediable material breach, give written particulars and 14 calendar days to remedy before termination. The parties coordinate migration or takedown instructions, outstanding receipts and final reporting. No platform processing deadline or preservation of playlists, identifiers or service data is guaranteed. Urgent rights violations may require proportionate suspension with notice as soon as reasonably practicable. Ending access does not erase signed records, accrued payment obligations or mandatory legal rights. Notice and cure periods are proposed business choices requiring approval.
common.studio access: Agreement-only access is available during onboarding. The {{studio_plan}} workspace is included after both signatures and final Control Center activation review, without a separate subscription charge for the included scope. Unreleased features, financial services, custom development and separately commissioned work are not promised. Included workspace access ends under the agreed exit arrangements; signed records and mandatory account rights remain available through an appropriate restricted route. Any later paid subscription requires a separate explicit purchase, never an automatic charge.
common.signing policy: Present the same fixed document and schedules to both verified signers. Record explicit intent and consent to sign, the document digest, reviewed sections, initials, signature evidence, signer account and server timestamps. Allow review and correction before confirmation. Provide each party the completed PDF and preserve the immutable version and audit events under a reviewed retention policy; confirm the applicable retention schedule before issuance. An image saved in a signature library does not sign any document. This internal process is not represented as qualified electronic signing or certified timestamping. No execution is recorded until the real issuing and evidence workflow is operational. Changes require a new fixed version and renewed acceptance. Each party may request a copy of its executed record.

silver.services: Release intake and quality review of supplied masters, artwork, metadata, credits and rights information; a dated correction and approval checklist; agreed catalogue presentation and release-administration tasks for accepted recordings. The release schedule identifies responsible persons, target dates, approval and revision limits before delivery. Production, mastering, legal clearances, paid promotion, PR, videos, standalone websites and domains are not included automatically. No service acceptance, placement, streams or income is guaranteed.

gold.services: Silver foundations plus an agreed release brief, asset checklist, positioning and organic campaign guidance, named responsibilities, campaign calendar and a review of available post-release data. A standalone website is eligible for separate scoping, not automatically commissioned. Any website schedule must identify pages, revisions, hosting, domain ownership, maintenance, costs and handover. Paid advertising and external PR require a separate approved budget. Review frequency, milestones and delivery limits must be agreed per project; no unlimited support or commercial outcome is promised.

platinum.services: Gold foundations plus scoped project leadership, release-calendar and campaign coordination, creative-direction planning and artist-development reviews. A project schedule identifies release count, team responsibilities, milestones, strategic-review frequency, artist approvals, revision limits and completion evidence. Website planning receives priority within an agreed scope; a build, hosting, domains and continuing maintenance are not automatic. Advances, paid media, third-party production and other investment require separate written funding and recoupment terms. No unlimited retainer, placement, audience, income or career outcome is promised.

sections.title: 1. Parties and authority
sections.text: Label contracting party: {{label_legal_name}}. Legal capacity, registration number where applicable and registered address: {{label_details}}. Authorized representative: {{label_signatory}}. Artist contracting party: {{artist_legal_name}}, professionally known as {{artist_name}}, with address and capacity: {{artist_details}}. Each signatory's authority must be verified before issuance. Artanrecords is the label brand, not a substitute for identifying the legal contracting party.

sections.title: 2. Covered recordings and services
sections.text: This draft concerns only the recordings identified in Schedule A: {{recordings}}. Agreed services and deliverables: {{services}}. No unrelated release, future work or service is included unless expressly identified in the final agreement. Release dates, platform delivery and third-party acceptance remain subject to the agreed release plan and applicable service requirements; no placement, stream count or income is guaranteed.

sections.title: 3. Term, territory and rights
sections.text: Effective date: {{effective_date}}. Contract term and renewal provisions: {{term}}. Territory: {{territory}}. Rights granted, exclusivity, permissions, sublicensing and post-termination treatment: {{rights}}. No transfer of master ownership or publishing rights is inferred from the partnership name or revenue allocation. Any grant must be expressly stated in the reviewed final rights schedule.

sections.title: 4. Recording-income allocation
sections.text: Proposed {{tier}} allocation: Artist {{artist_share}}%; Artanrecords {{label_share}}%. These are the canonical default recording allocations, commercial terms version {{commercial_version}}, and become contractual only in the final executed version. The basis is Eligible Net Master Receipts: actual recording receipts for the covered recordings, after reported adjustments and only deductions specifically allowed by the final agreement. Permitted deductions, exclusions, currency treatment and recoupment, if any: {{deductions}}. Do not apply this allocation to gross DSP estimates, publishing, merchandise, Store sales or Studio subscriptions.

sections.title: 5. Project Artist Pool and collaborators
sections.text: The Artist's {{artist_share}}% allocation forms the Project Artist Pool before any separately executed contributor allocations. Collaborator credit alone creates no revenue entitlement. Any contributor participation requires a separate agreement identifying the contributor, covered work, percentage, effective dates and revenue basis; it must not silently reduce Artanrecords' {{label_share}}% share. Applicable contributor schedule, if any: {{contributors}}.

sections.title: 6. Reporting, payment and tax
sections.text: Reporting frequency, statement delivery, payment timing, currency, withdrawal minimum where applicable, reserves, refunds, verification requirements and any approved fees: {{reporting_payment}}. No dashboard estimate is a verified payable balance. Tax responsibility and any legally required withholding: {{tax}}. This draft does not establish an internal wallet or authorize bank transfers, charges or withdrawals.

sections.title: 7. Materials, approvals and responsibilities
sections.text: The final agreement must identify delivery specifications, rights clearances, credits, artwork permissions, artist approvals and each party's responsibilities: {{responsibilities}}. Content declarations and any warranties or liability allocation require legal review. No broader warranty, indemnity or ownership declaration is inferred by the software.

sections.title: 8. Changes, ending the relationship and disputes
sections.text: Amendments require a new fixed version and renewed acceptance where appropriate; the signed historical version must remain unchanged. Termination rights, notice, cure periods, takedown handling and continuing reporting obligations: {{termination}}. Governing law, jurisdiction and dispute procedure: {{governing_law}}. These provisions must be completed by an authorized legal reviewer before the agreement can be issued.

sections.title: 9. Studio access and activation
sections.text: Included software access, its start and end dates, and service scope: {{studio_access}}. A tier request, selection, draft preview or proposed agreement does not activate a partnership. Activation requires the fixed reviewed agreement, authenticated signatures of both parties, explicit signing consent, server-recorded evidence and final authorized confirmation. Activation must reference that exact agreement version and cannot create financial payout eligibility by itself.

sections.title: 10. Electronic signing and records
sections.text: The final signing procedure must present the exact document and schedules, allow review and questions, record affirmative consent, bind each authenticated signer to the document digest, and preserve the signed record and event history. Agreed signature assurance, verification method and records policy: {{signing_policy}}. A typed name, uploaded image or preview alone is not proof that this agreement has been executed.
